Scope: these are the reviewed examples, not a completed repository-wide audit. Shared-result edges identify an output-lifetime concern, not proof that current callers retain stale results. Missing edges do not certify encapsulation.

Constructors such as DockTimer.new() and Bob.new(), constant reads, ordinary function calls, and independently owned SDK objects are excluded. The earlier scene-reference cycles are not counted as ownership violations.

This includes constructors, constant reads, calls, and scene navigation. It does not classify violations or count problematic cycles.

How this is built

Ownership findings are manually traced and backed by source anchors checked during generation. The lexical reference scanner alone cannot establish ownership, resolve object aliases, or detect escaped scratch buffers. The broader audits are recorded in the task list.

The background graph scans source/**/*.lua, excluding comments, strings, and self-references. Local aliases contribute references at their assignments. Passed instances and callbacks are not resolved. SDK and Lua built-ins are not individually audited here.

Rebuild with python3 tools/dependencies/build.py. Source listings and line numbers are embedded; no network libraries required.
